fixes.explanation: True, friend. God says, "I dispersed them among the nations, and they were scattered throughout the lands." He adds, "I judged them according to their ways and deeds." I think this one hurts.

This one's actually True, friend. The verse says, "I dispersed them among the nations, and they were scattered throughout the lands." That's God scattering them after He poured out His wrath (Ezekiel 36:18–19). The verse also says He judged them according to their ways and deeds. I think this one hurts.

That's the one, baker. Wherever they went, it was said of them, "These are the people of the LORD, yet they had to leave His land." God says that wherever they went, they profaned His holy name. I think that's a lot to carry around, being the walking headline.

Easy one to pick, baker, but this one's False. God says, "It is not for your sake that I will act, O house of Israel, but for My holy name, which you profaned among the nations to which you went." His message is about His name. Read it slow and you can hear it in the words.

That's it, baker. God says, "Then the nations will know that I am the LORD, declares the Lord GOD…" He says this will happen when He shows His holiness in Israel before their eyes. The knowing is about Him, not about anybody else.

I wish it worked on a pile of dirty mixing bowls, baker, but no. The word is idols. God says, "I will cleanse you from all your impurities and all your idols." It ties right back to verse 18, where idols defiled the land.

That's the one, baker. God says, "Then you will remember your evil ways and wicked deeds, and you will loathe yourselves for your iniquities and abominations." Loathe is a strong word, and it's the one God uses. Hate fits, because it's how they will feel about themselves.

That would be a plot twist, baker, but no. God says they will "…loathe yourselves for your iniquities and abominations." Loathing is the opposite of praise. They will remember their evil ways and wicked deeds, and they will loathe themselves.
Right, baker. God says, "Be ashamed and disgraced for your ways, O house of Israel!" It comes right after "It is not for your sake that I will act…" I think this is a heavy verse.

Yes, baker. The people will say, "This land that was desolate has become like the garden of Eden." Genesis 2:8 says God planted a garden in Eden, in the east. So the desolate land is going to be compared to that garden.
Uzza isn't the name Ezekiel uses, baker. The people say the land has become "…like the garden of Eden." Genesis 2:8 says God planted a garden in Eden, in the east. That's the name to remember.

Gethsemane is a real place, baker. It's where Jesus went to pray (Matthew 26:36), and He was arrested there afterward (Matthew 26:47–50). But it's not the garden in this verse. The people say the land has become "…like the garden of Eden."
That's it, baker. God says, "Once again I will hear the plea of the house of Israel…" A plea is a request made to Him. And "once again" tells me they've been heard by Him before.
